newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 16.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 16.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Wednesday and main factors likely to affect trading:

* Manila shares are likely to struggle higher encouraged by the uptickin the Dow Jones and PLDT's American Depositary Receipt but gains may not be supported by volume, Raul Ruiz, vice-president at Sun Hung Kai Securities said.
* BPI Securities Corp analyst Bernadette Tamayo advises investors to slowly accumulate oversold issues until clearer signs of a reversal are seen.

* Sun Hung Kai's Ruiz said investors may turn cautious on San Miguel Corp shares as the Presidential Commission on Good Government (PCGG), which holds majority shares in the food and beverage company, said it is urging San Miguel to seek better terms on a proposed merger deal with Coca-Cola Amatil.

* San Miguel stockholders approved on Tuesday plans to merge its unit Coca-Cola Bottlers Philipppines Inc with Australia's Coca-Cola Amatil. In exchange, San Miguel will get a 25 percent stake in Coca-Cola Amatil. The PCGG said though the government backed the merger, San Miguel should insist on increased representation in the Amatil board.
* On Tuesday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index closed higher by 16.62 points to 2,949.46.
* On Tuesday, the Dow Jones rose 135.26 points to 6,587.16. PLDT's ADR shed $0 1/4 to $58 3/4.
* Ayala Land Inc said it posted a 1.42 billion peso net income for the first quarter of 1997, from 1.24 billion in the same period last year.
* Guoco Holdings (Philippines) Inc said it has acquired a total of 82.4 percent interest in Pepsi Cola Products Philippines Inc.
* Newspaper Manila Times reports that PLDT sees interconnection problems with other phone companies resolved by the second quarter of the year.
* The peso closed higher at 26.359 to the dollar vs 26.362.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was unchanged at 10.03125 percent.
